title: Management of Information Technology
description: Strategic use and impact of information technology (IT) in organizations. Covers what IT is, and how it works, business value of IT, and IT strategies that organizations can employ to create value.
prerequisites_raw: MGMT 107

title: Supply Chain Management
description: Flows of materials and information among all of the firms that contribute to a product or service. Forecasting, demand management, logistical networks, inventory management, supplier contracting, sourcing, information technology, flexibility, globalization, and performance management.
prerequisites_raw: MGMT 7

title: Business Process Management
description: Learn core business functions, processes, and data requirements to support complex interrelationships between procurement, sales, and logistics. Hands-on experience with enterprise resource planning, sales and operations planning, material requirements planning, master scheduling, and aggregate planning.

title: Operations Management
description: Managing the productive resources, from which raw materials as inputs are being transformed into useful outputs of final products and services. Explanation of issues pertaining to both manufacturing and services-oriented systems.
prerequisites_raw: MGMT 7

title: Special Topics in Management
description: Studies in selected areas of management. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Business Communication
description: Provides students with a solid foundation in business communication. Emphasis is placed on improving students' written and oral communication skills to help them succeed in (1) upper-division Business Administration courses, (2) graduate school, and (3) work and career activities.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Business Law
description: A study of the legal environment of business. Topics include contracts, agency, partnerships, corporations, and other basic principles of law as they relate to business transactions.

title: Financial Statement Analysis
description: Study of financial statements and their related footnotes; tools and procedures common to financial statement analysis; relationships among business transactions, environmental forces (political, economic, social), and reported financial statement information; how financial statement information can help solve certain business problems.
prerequisites_raw: MGMT 30A

title: Experiential Development of a Global Business Perspective
description: Opportunity for students to consider historical and modern global businesses, governmental, and non-profit operations in Switzerland. Effectively provides live case studies for analysis of global interrelatedness. Materials Fee

title: Decision Analysis
description: Use of decision analysis digital technologies for multiple objective decisions under certainty; decision-making under risk using decision trees; fitting probability distributions to judgments or data; and Monte Carlo simulation, applied to business, government, not-for-profit, and personal decisions.
prerequisites_raw: MGMT 101

title: Predictive Analytics
description: Addresses prediction and classification problems in the management context via statistical learning. Provides an overview of modern methodologies in forecasting and data mining including multiple regression, decision trees, logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor, support vector machines, and neural nets.
prerequisites_raw: MGMT 101

title: Administrative Internship
description: Selected undergraduates serve as managers within administrative units on campus with a three-quarter course which complements the intern experience. Topics include management ethics, study of non- and for-profit institutions, career management, and the changing nature of the workforce.

title: Administrative Internship
description: Selected undergraduates serve as managers within administrative units on campus with a three-quarter course which complements the intern experience. Topics include management ethics, study of non- and for-profit institutions, career management, and the changing nature of the workforce.

description: Independent research within the laboratories of graduate training faculty in the Department of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry for first-year Ph.D. students.

title: Seminars in Molecular Biology & Biochemistry
description: Presentation of research from department laboratories or, when pertinent, of other recent developments.

title: Nucleic Acid Structure and Function
description: Structure and chemistry of nucleic acids. Relationship between these properties and the mechanisms of fundamental processes such as replication and repair, RNA-mediated catalysis, formation and regulation of higher order chromatin structure and recombination.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and CHEM 51A and CHEM 51B and CHEM 51C

title: Protein Structure and Function
description: The structure and properties of proteins, enzymes, and their kinetic properties.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 98 and BIO SCI 99 and CHEM 51C

title: Molecular Virology
description: Primary research data on the major DNA and RNA viruses emphasizing strategies of regulation of gene expression. Utilization of viruses as molecular biological tools. Graduate-level knowledge of the biochemistry and molecular biology of macromolecules is required.
prerequisites_raw: MOL BIO 203 with a minimum grade of B- and MOL BIO 204 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Tumor Microenvironment, Immunology, and Metabolism
description: Covers basic background and current topics in the cells that compose the complex tumor microenvironment. Explores how these cells interact to support metabolism and shape immune response.

title: Structural Biology
description: Basic principles of magnetic resonance, Xray crystallography, and CryoEM toward the determination of high-resolution biomolecular structures.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 2B

title: Literature in Protein Structure and Function
description: Exploration and critical analysis of recent primary scientific literature in structure and properties of proteins, enzymes, and their kinetic properties.

title: Integrative Immunology I
description: Provides an introduction to immunology, but focuses on providing in-depth analysis of selected topics within the broader field of immunology, including relevant research techniques, while improving critical thinking skills.

title: Integrative Immunology II
description: Lectures and student presentations of primary literature. Focuses on advanced topics and cutting edge technologies in modern immunology. Combination of didactic lectures and student-led journal article discussion.
prerequisites_raw: PHYSIO 215 with a minimum grade of B+

title: Principles of Cancer Biology I
description: Oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes are studied from molecular viewpoints. Also studies their role in cancer; viral carcinogenesis. Designed for graduate students interested in cancer research. Format includes lectures and student-led discussions.
prerequisites_raw: MOL BIO 203 with a minimum grade of B- and MOL BIO 204 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Principles of Cancer Biology II
description: Topics include cancer cell growth and metastasis, chemical carcinogenesis, and cancer genetics and epidemiology. Designed for graduate students interested in cancer research. Format includes lectures and student-led discussions.
prerequisites_raw: MOL BIO 203 with a minimum grade of B- and MOL BIO 204 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Clinical Cancer
description: Designed to acquaint students in basic life science with clinical cancer.

title: Structure & Synthesis of Biological Macromolecules Journal Club
description: Advanced topics in macromolecular struture and synthesis as related to biological problems.

title: Advanced Immunology Laboratory
description: An advanced course in immunology for graduate students enrolled in the Biotechnology master's program. Emphasis is placed on learning modern techniques in immunology such as ELISAs, western blotting, immunofluorescent staining assays.

title: Introduction to Computational Biology
description: The use of theories and methods based on computer science, mathematics, and physics in molecular biology and biochemistry. Basics in biomolecular modeling. Analysis of sequence and structural data of biomolecules. Analysis of biomolecular functions.

title: Immunology Journal Club
description: Advanced topics in immunology as related to an understanding of human disease.

title: Research-in-Progress Seminars
description: Two half-hour presentations by graduate students and postdoctorals to the department on their current research projects.

title: Muscle Journal Club and Research in Progress
description: Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of current research and advancements in the field of skeletal muscle biology and disease.

title: Topics in Stem Cells
description: Presentation by participating faculty or guest lecturer that is open to the science community, followed by discussion of the lecture topic or a related topic. Students are responsible for presentations and readings.

title: Metallobiochemistry
description: A review of the biochemistry of metallic elements emphasizing: methods for studying metals in biological systems; the chemical basis for nature's exploitation of specific elements; structures of active sites; mechanisms; solid-state structures and devices; metals in medicine.
prerequisites_raw: CHEM 131C (may be taken concurrently) or CHEM 132C (may be taken concurrently)

title: Advanced Topics in Biotechnology - Nucleic Acids
description: Supplements laboratory curriculum with scientific background behind experimental methods. Format consists of lectures and the presentation and analysis of relevant papers from the scientific literature.

title: Biotechnology Laboratory - Nucleic Acids
description: Nucleic acid techniques and recombinant DNA technology. Extraction and purification of nucleic acids, cloning and subcloning, PCR, site-directed mutagenesis, nucleic acid hybridization, additional associated procedures. Students must demonstrate accurate documentation of data (laboratory notebook) detailing experience and results.

title: Advanced Topics in Biotechnology - Protein Purification and Characterization
description: Supplements laboratory curriculum with scientific background behind experimental methods. Format consists of lectures and the presentation and analysis of relevant papers from the scientific literature.
prerequisites_raw: MOL BIO 250L with a minimum grade of B- and MOL BIO 250 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Biotechnology Laboratory - Protein Purification and Characterization
description: Major techniques of handling proteins and antibodies. Protein engineering, expression and large-scale purification of recombinant proteins from bacteria, HPLC, antibody purification, western blotting, additional associated procedures. Students must demonstrate accurate documentation of data (laboratory notebook) detailing experience and results.
prerequisites_raw: MOL BIO 250L with a minimum grade of B- and MOL BIO 250 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Biotechnology Management Laboratory
description: Overview of current methods in biotechnology, designed specifically for biotechnology graduate students. Organized into four distinct sections (nucleic acids, proteins, virology, and immunology). Students must demonstrate accurate documentation of data (laboratory notebooks) detailing experience and results.

title: Biotech Management
description: Taught jointly by Bio Sci and Merage School faculty, the course addresses fundamental aspects within, and associated with, the biotechnology industry. Curriculum is focused largely on management issues, including finance, product development, pharmaceuticals, project management, regulatory affairs, and ethics.

title: Seminar in Systems Microbiology Research
description: A research and journal club seminar that covers topics on bacteria and phage using approaches and principles from biology, engineering, and physics.

title: Science Communication Skills
description: Development of effective communication skills, oral and written presentations. Topics range from the art of creating keynote slides to strategically crafting a personal story, culminating in a live presentation to an invited audience.

title: Advanced Cryogenic Electron Microscopy
description: Electron microscopy for biological applications. Practical aspects of cryo-EM, including sample preparation, instrumentation, data collection and processing methods. Electron crystallography, tomography and microED. Applications of cryo-EM, current issues and future avenues are discussed along with computational protein design.

title: Advanced Topics in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
description: Selected topics in specified areas of concentration, e.g., nucleic acids, protein biochemistry, genetic expression, biochemical genetics. Specific topics announced in advance.

title: Graduate School Fundamentals
description: Lectures and discussions providing basic skills needed for success in Ph.D. graduate studies. Topics include formulating a hypothesis, experimental design, literature review, grant writing, oral communication, biostatistics, time management, and professional development.

title: Scientific Communication
description: Small group meetings for graduate students to practice scientific writing, debate, and presentation skills.

title: Scientific Communication

title: Cancer Biology Journal Club
description: Focuses on molecular mechanisms that underlie the development and progression of cancers. Covers a variety of cancer-related research areas, such as cell cycle control, apoptosis, DNA repair, metastasis, angiogenesis, and others.

title: Cancer Biology Journal Club
description: Focuses on molecular mechanisms that underlie the development and progression of cancers. Covers a variety of cancer-related research areas, such as cell cycle control, apoptosis, DNA repair, metastasis, angiogenesis, and others.

title: Cancer Biology Journal Club
description: Focuses on molecular mechanisms that underlie the development and progression of cancers. Covers a variety of cancer-related research areas, such as cell cycle control, apoptosis, DNA repair, metastasis, angiogenesis, and others.

title: Computer and Communication Networks
description: Network architecture of the Internet, telephone networks, cable networks, and cell phone networks. Network performance models. Network performance models. Advanced concepts and implementations of flow and congestion control, addressing, internetworking, forwarding, routing, multiple access, streaming, and quality-of-service.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 148 or COMPSCI 132

title: Networking Laboratory
description: A laboratory-based introduction to basic networking concepts such as addressing, sub-netting, bridging, ARP, and routing. Network simulation and design. Structured around weekly readings and laboratory assignments.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 148 or COMPSCI 132

title: Advanced Networks
description: Design principles of networked systems, advanced routing and congestion control algorithms, network algorithms, network measurement, management, security, Internet economics, and emerging networks.
prerequisites_raw: NET SYS 201 with a minimum grade of B- or COMPSCI 232 with a minimum grade of B- or EECS 248A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Wireless and Mobile Networking
description: Introduction to wireless networking. The focus is on layers 2 and 3 of the OSI reference model, design, performance analysis, and protocols. Topics covered include: an introduction to wireless networking, digital cellular, next generation cellular, wireless LANs, and mobile IP.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 148 or COMPSCI 132

title: Network and Distributed Systems Security
description: Modern computer and networks security: attacks and countermeasures, authentication, identification, data secrecy, data integrity, authorization, access control, computer viruses, network security. Group communication and multicast security techniques. Covers secure e-commerce and applications of public key methods, digital certificates, and credentials.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 148 or COMPSCI 132

title: Middleware for Networked and Distributed Systems
description: Discusses concepts, techniques, and issues in developing distributed systems middleware that provides high performance and Quality of Service for emerging applications. Also covers existing standards (e.g., CORBA, DCOM, Jini, Espeak) and their relative advantages and shortcomings.
prerequisites_raw: An undergraduate-level course in operating systems and networks

title: Topics in Networked Systems
description: Study of Networked concepts.

title: California Teach 1: Introduction to Science and Mathematics Teaching
description: First in a series for students interested in becoming middle or high school teachers of mathematics or science. Students gain an understanding of effective, research-based teaching strategies. Includes supervised field experience in a K-12 classroom.

title: Introduction to Computation for Scientists and Engineers
description: Introduces principles, techniques, and computational tools for quantitative approach to basic problem solving in physics and engineering. Project-based course that actively explores how programming techniques are used for solving STEM real-world problems.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 2A (may be taken concurrently) or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 3

title: Skills Development
description: Undergraduates identify, cultivate, and practice relevant soft skills applicable to careers in mathematics and science. The focus is on career readiness, how to market oneself to future employers, and what to expect from the professional world.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: California Teach 2: Middle School Science and Mathematics Teaching
description: Second in a series for students interested in becoming middle or high school teachers of mathematics or science. Students gain an understanding of effective, research-based teaching strategies for grades 6-8. Includes supervised field experience in a middle school classroom.
prerequisites_raw: PHY SCI 5 or BIO SCI 14

title: Technical Writing and Communication Skills
description: Workshop in writing technical reports, journal articles, proposals. Oral presentations. Communicating with the public. May not be used in satisfaction of any School or departmental requirement.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Introduction to Sociology
description: Considers major sociological concepts, theories, and research findings illuminating processes of interpersonal interaction, social differentiation and stratification, integration and conflict, and change, with attention to variation in class, race/ethnic, gender, multicultural, and cross-national perspectives and experiences.

title: Globalization
description: Examines globalization and international issues from the perspective of sociology and related fields. Issues include economic globalization and global inequality, international environmental problems, international politics, trends in global culture, and global conflict.

title: Social Problems
description: Focuses on how institutional and organizational features of societies generate problems for people. Particular attention directed at a set of problems related to political and economic inequality: poverty, racism, sexism, urban and population problems, the environment, the criminal justice system.

title: Probability and Statistics
description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on a thorough understanding of the probabilistic basis of statistical inference. Emphasizes examples from sociology, anthropology, and related social science disciplines.

title: Probability and Statistics
description: An introduction to probability and statistics. Emphasis on a thorough understanding of the probabilistic basis of statistical inference. Emphasizes examples from sociology, anthropology, and related social science disciplines.
prerequisites_raw: SOCIOL 10A or ANTHRO 10A

title: Self-Identity and Society
description: Studies sociological contributions to theory and research in social psychology, with focus on the social influences on personality, attitudes, beliefs, and behavior; socialization, human groups, and social interaction.

title: Special Topics: Social Psychology
description: Studies in selected areas of social psychology. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Small Group Dynamics
description: Deals with models for understanding behavior in small groups, including coalition formation, socialization, group norms and decision rules, leadership, conformity, group structure, and communication processes.

title: City and Community
description: Examines nature, causes, and consequences of urbanization along with changing scale and complexity, demographic/ecological city growth patterns, quality of life in urban areas, processes of decision-making, and bearing of sociological investigation on public policy concerns in contemporary urban society.

title: Births, Deaths, and Migration
description: Introduction to the analysis of human population including fertility, mortality dispersion, sex distribution. Attention is focused on the effects of these variables on, e.g., over-population, social disorganization, and the stability of social institutions.

title: Asian American Family & Community
description: Briefly examines the history of different Asian American groups and provides an in-depth analysis of issues related to family composition, mate selection, changing gender roles, and intergenerational conflict.

title: Disability in Society
description: Explores issues around disability in society, including the central place that ableism plays in contemporary societies and the implications of categorizing certain bodies as disabled for social inequality.

title: Religion and Society
description: A critical and personal examination of the varieties of religious and spiritual experiences human beings are undergoing in contemporary society. The role of conscious understanding and unconscious conditioning regarding religion and spirituality.

title: Special Topics: Social Institutions and Culture
description: Studies in selected areas of social institutions and culture. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Families and Intimate Relations
description: Sociological theories/research on marriage, kinship, intimacy, and divorce. Emphasis on comparing family patterns in different social classes, ethnic groups, and societies, and on relating family life to the economy and other social institutions. Topics include gender roles, child-rearing, historical change.

title: Race and Ethnicity
description: Focuses on racial and ethnic relations in the United States and compares them with those found in other societies. Analyzes the conditions that favor either cooperation and integration or rivalry, tension, and conflict. Appraises strategies for reducing and resolving conflicts.

title: Sociology of Sexuality
description: Provides an introduction to and overview of the sociology of sex and sexuality. Considers the social meanings of sex and sexuality, the social contexts of sex and sexuality, and the social regulations of sex and sexuality.

title: Gender and Race Inequality in the Workplace
description: Analysis of current state and trends in major inequality measures including the wage gap, occupational segregation, and access to managerial positions. Theories that purport to explain such differences, and the related empirical evidence, are also covered.

title: Ethnic and Immigrant America
description: Focusing on Asian, Latino, and Black immigrant groups, examines the second generation's experience of straddling two cultures and growing up American. Covers topics such as assimilation, bilingualism, race relations, education, bicultural conflicts, interracial marriage, and multiracial identities.

title: Special Topics: Age, Gender, Race, and Ethnicity
description: Studies in selected areas of age, gender, race, and ethnicity. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Special Topics: Societies and Social Inequality
description: Studies in selected areas of societies and social inequality. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Research Methods
description: Methods of data collection and analysis used by sociologists. Experimental methods, surveys, and interviews, field research and participant observation, demographic methods, historical and comparative approaches.

title: Special Topics: Methods
description: Studies in selected areas of methods. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Sociological Theory
description: What a theory of society is and is not. Historical and contemporary models, perspectives, and schools.

title: Game Theory and Politics I
description: Introduction to game theory and a survey of its political applications. Examples of topics covered include voting in small committees, legislatures, and mass elections; interest group activities and environmental issues; institutional design, and the evolution of cooperative behavior.

title: Social Psychology of Networks
description: Review of network methods used in small group and organizational research. Discussion of social psychological literature relevant to the network of study of cognitive social structure, exchange/communication, identity negotiation, and social control. Case study of network datasets exemplifies research issues.

title: Business Decisions
description: Surveys normative and descriptive models of decision-making behavior, with an emphasis on organizational and policy contexts. Topics include rational choice theory, biases and heuristics, framing effects, and overconfidence. Management fads, panics, and herd behavior are also discussed.
prerequisites_raw: ( ANTHRO 10A and ANTHRO 10B and ANTHRO 10C ) or ( SOCIOL 10A and SOCIOL 10B and SOCIOL 10C ) or ( SOC SCI 10A and SOC SCI 10B and SOC SCI 10C ) or ( MATH 2A and MATH 2B and ( STATS 7 or MGMT 7 ) or ( STATS 120A and STATS 120B and STATS 120C ) or ( ECON 15 or ECON 15B or MATH 130B )

title: Organizations
description: How bureaucracies, formal organizations, and voluntary associations work, how/why they grow, and where they are going. History and structure of organizational rationality; dynamics of organized groups; behavior in organizations; limits of bureaucratization and attempts to overcome these limits through decentralization.

title: White-Collar Crime
description: Examines criminal activity in business and corporate enterprise, organizations, and the professions. Theories regarding the causes and control of white-collar and corporate crime are covered as well as the numerous definitions of these terms.

title: Social Networks and Social Support
description: Examines the manner in which behaviors/attitudes of individuals are affected by their network ties to others. How are peoples' opportunities and well-being increased/decreased by their social networks? May include studies in mental/physical health, job seeking, separation and loss, and aging.

title: Politics, Power, and Society
description: Includes an examination of the major theoretical approaches to political sociology, and the application of these ideas to the politics of advanced capitalist societies. Also considers stability and change in power structures.

title: PrisonPandemic: Understanding Incarcerated People’s Pandemic Experiences
description: Focuses on experiences shared by people incarcerated during the COVID-19 pandemic and helps students learn skills for interacting with archival materials and actively engaging with the sociohistorical context and modern critiques of the U.S. carceral system.

title: Special Topics: Structures
description: Studies in selected areas of structures. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Sociological Lens on Religion
description: Examines the effects of religious beliefs, belonging, and institutions on social dynamics, including class, gender, and racial stratification, politics, and social movements. Additional topics: the sociological significance of conversion, commitment, and secularization/sacralization.

title: Social Inequalities and Health
description: Introduces ways in which social inequalities produce health disparities. Begins with general perspectives on social causation of health, and then considers how particular individual attributes (e.g., gender, SES, race/ethnicity, nativity) and social contexts (e.g., neighborhoods) can get “under the skin.”

title: Global Peace
description: Why do countries fight wars? Will world peace ever be possible? Focuses on social structures that might lead to global peace, with an emphasis on the role of culture and narrative in bringing peace locally, nationally, and globally.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Medical Sociology
description: Current problems in U.S. health-care system and proposals for reform. Examines financial barriers to access; problem of patient dumping; underinsurance; prenatal and perinatal care; child services; preventative care and needs of the elderly; minorities; low-income people; undocumented.

title: Baseball and Society
description: An examination of baseball's role in American social life over the last 150 years. Issues of fraternal organizations, national development, capitalism, rationalization, race and ethnicity, gender, economic organization, labor relations, and politics are discussed.

title: Baseball and Society
description: An examination of baseball's role in American social life over the last 150 years. Issues of fraternal organizations, national development, capitalism, rationalization, race and ethnicity, gender, economic organization, labor relations, and politics are discussed.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Deviance
description: Perspectives on deviance and criminality in behavior, institution, community, and myth. The suitability of contemporary theories of deviant behavior.

title: Sociology of Education
description: Focuses on education’s role in creating and redressing inequality, and in shaping how we understand our place in society. Education from cross-national and historical perspectives, and education as a vehicle for examining and solving social problems.

title: Sociology of Education
description: Focuses on education’s role in creating and redressing inequality, and in shaping how we understand our place in society. Education from cross-national and historical perspectives, and education as a vehicle for examining and solving social problems.

title: Comparing European and US Societies
description: Society, culture, institutions of U.S. and European countries. Fertility to football, guns to government, work to welfare, health to housework. Cross-national approaches for understanding the world and thinking critically about taken-for-granted practices. Policies the U.S. might borrow for social issues.

title: Sociology of Mental Health
description: Examines the social causes, consequences, and patterns of mental health and illness. Students learn a sociological perspective on mental health, mental illness or disorder, and medicine/health care, ranging from social definitions, roles, and interactions to societal stratification and international patterns.

title: Money, Work, and Social Life
description: Sociological perspective on issues related to money and work. Consumption practices and lifestyles, jobs and organizations, issues of money in intimate relations, marriage, and households, illegal work, discrimination, economic globalization are discussed.

title: Money, Work, and Social Life
description: Sociological perspective on issues related to money and work. Consumption practices and lifestyles, jobs and organizations, issues of money in intimate relations, marriage, and households, illegal work, discrimination, economic globalization are discussed.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Special Topics: Social Institutions and Culture
description: Studies in selected areas of social institutions and culture. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Sociology of Sex and Gender
description: Explores complex processes contributing to social construction of gender and sexuality in the U.S. with focus on intersection of gender, race, ethnicity, sexuality, and class; evaluates how men and women are differentially constituted in family, education, work, politics, media, language.

title: Sociology of Sex and Gender
description: Explores complex processes contributing to social construction of gender and sexuality in the U.S. with focus on intersection of gender, race, ethnicity, sexuality, and class; evaluates how men and women are differentially constituted in family, education, work, politics, media, language.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Gender and Ethnicity: Chicana/Latina Feminisms in the US
description: Focuses on the Latina Feminist Group and testimonios to examine the historical development of Chicana/Latinx feminist thought and practice. Draws from interdisciplinary scholarship to survey the diversity of contemporary Chicana/Latinx feminisms through an intersectionality lens.

title: Credit, Debt, and Inequality
description: Examines the influence social background has on net worth. Engages sociological texts to understand the causes and consequences of credit and debt for inequality in the U.S.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Sociology of Aging
description: Introduction to sociology of age, aging, and the aged. Problems posed by aging population. Life course transitions and how social organizations influence the life course. Addresses work, health, and family in later life.

title: Immigration and Inequality
description: Explores immigration, ethnicity, and inequality as interconnected social forces. International migration, propelled by global inequalities, plays a central role in the formation of multinational societies, shapes inter-group relations and patterns of ethnic inequality, and transforms the immigrants themselves.

title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.

title: Racial and Ethnic Relations in the United States
description: Examines central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity; the emergence, maintenance, and consequences of the ethnic and racial stratification system in the United States; the future of racial and ethnic relations; and relevant public policy issues.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Neighborhood Inequality and Residential Segregation
description: Examine how legacies of residential segregation continue to permeate areas of U.S. social life. Engage sociological texts alongside related current events that describe, explain, and predict the causes and consequences of residential segregation for enduring racial inequality in the U.S.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Special Topics in Age, Gender, Race, and Ethnicity
description: Studies in selected areas of age, gender, race, and ethnicity. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Vietnam War
description: Examines social structures and social changes in Vietnamese and U.S. societies through the study of the Vietnam War.

title: U.S. War on Terrorism
description: Analyzes the United States war on terrorism by focusing on terrorism, the U.S. wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, and changes in police powers through the Patriot Act, as well as the political leadership which directs the war.

title: Environment and Society
description: Examines society's changing relationship to the natural world. Delineates different models of "nature" and then explores their institutional roots, the social responses they have generated, and their implications for social inequality.

title: Chicane/Latine Education
description: Provides a historical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting diverse Latine low-income, immigrant, and U.S. born student populations enrolled in American schools. Examines policies and issues such as DACA, generation, culture, racism, and gender on educational mobility.

title: Social Inequality
description: Sources, functions, and dynamics of the unequal distribution of wealth, prestige, knowledge, and power in American and other societies.

title: Sociology of Poverty
description: Examines the promise of social mobility and the roots of poverty in the United States with a focus on race, class, and gender.

title: Social Inequality
description: Sources, functions, and dynamics of the unequal distribution of wealth, prestige, knowledge, and power in American and other societies.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Protests, Movements, and Revolutions
description: A survey of models of collective action drawn from sociology, economics, psychology, and political science. Focus on areas such as social movements, strikes, crowd psychology, cults, fads, fashions, public opinion, and symbolic and mythical elements in collective culture.
prerequisites_raw: SOCIOL 1 or POL SCI 11A or ECON 1

title: China in the Global Age
description: Chinese society from 1949 to present. Social change in the context of political control and ideological considerations. Focus on the power structure, political decision processes, and ideological legitimation, and interplay with the Chinese community and its culture.

title: International Divided Cities
description: Investigates urban divisions in international cities where deep-seated nationalistic ethnic differences create pressures for intergroup conflicts, autonomy, or territorial separation, and can incite violence. Urban political polarization as it is manifest in the urban setting.

title: Immigration and Social Policy
description: Explains how people decide to migrate and how they are incorporated into a host society (both historically and currently), examines the effects of immigration on the U.S., analyzes how the framing of immigration shapes the discourse about the issue.

title: Undocumented Immigrant Experiences
description: Examines the experiences of undocumented immigrants and the policies that structure their educational, economic, social, and political participation.

title: Sociology of Human Rights
description: Focuses on human rights – the idea that everyone has fundamental rights by virtue of being a human person – as a sociological phenomenon.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Special Topics: Societies and Social Inequality
description: Studies in selected areas of societies and social inequality. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Sociology Majors Seminar
description: Students learn sociology by doing it. A modest-sized research project is planned and implemented by each student.
prerequisites_raw: SOCIOL 110

title: Sociology Majors Seminar
description: Students learn sociology by doing it. A modest-sized research project is planned and implemented by each student.
prerequisites_raw: SOCIOL 110 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Honors Research and Thesis
description: Focuses on the design and implementation of individual research projects undertaken by senior Sociology majors. Writing projects consist of a proposal and paper on some empirical research.
prerequisites_raw: SOCIOL H188A . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Honors Research and Thesis
description: Focuses on the design and implementation of individual research projects undertaken by senior Sociology majors. Writing projects consist of a proposal and paper on some empirical research.

title: Special Topics: Honors Sequence
description: Independent honors research with Social Sciences faculty.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Field Study
description: Field study with Sociology faculty.

title: Directed Group Study
description: Directed study with Sociology faculty.

title: Independent Study
description: Independent research with Sociology faculty.

title: Proseminar I in Sociology
description: Introduces first-year graduate students in Sociology to the current research interests of Sociology faculty, as well as to other aspects of graduate life at UCI and to the profession of sociology more generally.

title: Proseminar II in Sociology
description: Focus is on second-year research projects, design, development, data gathering, analysis, and preparing oral and written presentations of the results. Students learn analytic and writing skills, gain experience with research processes, and become socialized about professional standards, customs, and institutions.

title: Classical Social Theory
description: Examines the development of classical sociological theory through the writings of Karl Marx, Emile Durkheim, Max Weber, Georg Simmel, and George Herbert Mead.

title: Contemporary Social Theory
description: Familiarizes students with 20th-century developments in social thought that have influenced sociological research, suggesting "what is living and what is dead" in the "classics" and offering an overview of the main outlines of recent sociological theorizing.

title: Network Theory
description: An introduction to theoretical work in the field of social networks. Topics include baseline models, homphily, and propinquity, exchange and power, balance theory, diffusion and social influence, equivalence, and cohesion. Deductive use of theory to make novel predictions is emphasized.

title: Special Topics: Theory
description: Studies in selected areas of theory. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Research Design
description: Data collection, organization, and analysis in ethnographic or quasi-experimental settings, including interviewing, participant observations, behavior observations, and questionnaires. Research design issues include sampling, longitudinal research, and comparative research. Emphasis on the integration of qualitative and quantitative data.

title: Graduate Statistics I
description: Statistics with emphasis on applications in sociology and anthropology. Examines exploratory uses of statistical tools in these fields as well as univariate, bivariate, and multivariate applications in the context of the general linear model.

title: Graduate Statistics II
description: Statistics with emphasis on applications in sociology and anthropology. Examines exploratory uses of statistical tools in these fields as well as univariate, bivariate, and multivariate applications in the context of the general linear model.
prerequisites_raw: SOCIOL 221A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Graduate Statistics III
description: Statistics with emphasis on applications in sociology and anthropology. Examines exploratory uses of statistical tools in these fields as well as univariate, bivariate, and multivariate applications in the context of the general linear model.
prerequisites_raw: SOCIOL 221A with a minimum grade of B- and SOCIOL 221B with a minimum grade of B-

title: Comparative and Historical Sociological Methods
description: Topics include the logic of comparative and historical analysis techniques and the examination of exemplar works in representative problem areas.

title: Analyzing Qualitative Data
description: Focuses on analyzing interview and field note data to write argument-driven academic papers.
prerequisites_raw: ( SOCIOL 227A with a minimum grade of B- and SOCIOL 227B with a minimum grade of B-) or SOCIOL 224 with a minimum grade of B-. Required: At least 10-15 interview transcripts or field notes that correspond to at least 10-15 hours of ethnographic observation

title: Interview Methods
description: Hands-on introduction to the use of interviews in social scientific research. Topics include when to use interviews and/or focus groups; how to design an interview-based study, how to conduct interviews, analyze interview data, and write up and publish interview-based results.

title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
description: Introduces basic demographic methods used in social science and public health research. Topics include sources and limitations of demographic data; components of population growth; measures of nuptiality, fertility, mortality, and population mobility projection methods; and demographic models.

title: Seminar Ethnographic & Qualitative Field Methods
description: Comprehensive and critical discussion of the traditions of qualitative fieldwork; detailed examination of the collection, coding, analysis, and presentation of ethnographic/qualitative field data; and close mentoring of student projects culminating in an original research paper.

title: Seminar Ethnographic & Qualitative Field Methods
description: Comprehensive and critical discussion of the traditions of qualitative fieldwork; detailed examination of the collection, coding, analysis, and presentation of ethnographic/qualitative field data; and close mentoring of student projects culminating in an original research paper.
prerequisites_raw: SOCIOL 227A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Special Topics: Methods
description: Studies in selected areas of methods. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Race and Ethnicity
description: An examination of central questions and issues in the field of race and ethnicity through a critical analysis and discussion of the principal theoretical perspectives and paradigms that have framed much of the scholarship in the area.

title: Administrative Data Research
description: Provides a supportive environment for students using administrative data in research projects across a wide range of fields, including, but not limited to, public health, education, economics, psychology, political science, and sociology.

title: Race and Ethnicity Perspectives
description: Discusses current research on race and ethnicity in the social sciences that incorporates critical race perspectives with an emphasis on explanations of social inequality.

title: Ethnic America
description: Examines critically the meaning and measurement of ethnicity, race, and nation in sociological theory and research. Theories of ethnicity are explored, along with empirical studies of the construction of ethnic and pan-ethnic identities in historical and contemporary contexts.

title: Poverty and Development
description: Examines competing conceptualizations, methods of measurement, and poverty alleviation strategies widely used in developing countries. Focuses on poverty conceptualized as economic deprivation, well-being, vulnerability, and social exclusion.

title: Educational Inequality
description: Focuses on macro-level explanations of inequality of schooling, particularly in the U.S. context. Explores traditional models, such as conflict, functionalism, status-attainment, cultural reproduction, and newer synthetic accounts. Emphasis on higher education access and the intersection of education and work.

title: Special Topics: Social Inequality
description: Studies in selected areas of social inequality. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Social Movements
description: A survey of the field of Social Movements, oriented around critical themes in the major theoretical traditions and contemporary exemplars.

title: Political Sociology
description: Begins with an examination of the three major orientations to the State (Pluralist, Elitist, and Class). Next considers current topics in political sociology including the Welfare State, the New Deal, political behavior, social movements, participation, and democracy.

title: Sociology of Culture
description: Major perspectives in the sociology of culture. Topics include the role of cultural dynamics in the reproduction of inequality, collective action, political and organizational decision making, emotional experience, and the social impacts of new technologies.

title: Special Topics: Political Sociology and Social Movements
description: Studies in selected areas of political sociology and social movements. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Global Urbanization
description: Examines the spread of cities worldwide in the 20th century. What are the political and economic causes of this process? What are the social-cultural, political, and economic effects? How is contemporary urbanization linked to global restructuring of other kinds?

title: Special Topics: Global Studies and Comparative Development
description: Studies in selected areas of global studies and comparative development. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Population
description: Introduces the interrelationships between population and social organization. Considers measurement and explanation of historical and contemporary trends in birth rates, death rates, migration, and marriage and divorce. Case material is drawn primarily from the U.S. and other industrialized nations.

title: Immigrant America
description: The study of the causes and consequences of international migration has become one of the most vital fields of sociological theory and research. Examines principal theoretical perspectives and empirical research on contemporary immigration flows and the processes of incorporation.

title: DASA Research Design
description: Data collection, organization, and analysis in population studies and demography. Research design issues include sampling, longitudinal research, and comparative research.
prerequisites_raw: Enrollment in DASA program

title: Crimmigration
description: Examines the criminalization of immigration, with an emphasis on U.S. enforcement procedures and outcomes. Analyzes the devolution of federal immigration law to local authorities, the rise in immigrant detention and deportation, and the militarization of the U.S.-Mexico border.

title: Special Topics: Social Demography
description: Studies in selected areas of social demography. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Special Topics: Social Organizations and Institutions
description: Studies in selected areas of social organizations and institutions. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Analysis of Social Network Data
description: Overview and application of methods for analyzing social network data. Topics include: data structures, visualization, graph theory, centrality, subgroups, positions, blockmodels, local properties, and statistical models. Social network analysis software is used to analyze a range of examples.

title: Introduction to Social Networks
description: Provides a broad overview of the history, concepts, and applications of social networks. Students have the opportunity to delve deeply into applications of the network approach in their individual areas of interest.

title: Special Topics
description: Studies in selected areas of Social Sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Dissertation Research
description: Dissertation research with Sociology faculty.

title: The Art of Writing: Poetry
description: Beginners' workshop in the writing of poetry, evaluation of student manuscripts, and parallel readings.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement

title: The Art of Writing: Prose Fiction
description: Beginners' workshop in fiction writing, evaluation of student manuscripts, and parallel readings.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement

title: Introduction to Writing and Rhetoric
description: Introduction to the principles of rhetoric through readings and writing assignments across a range of genres, including fiction, non-fiction, journalism and academic essays. Rigorous instruction in composition and style, including organization, paragraph development, sentence-level mechanics.
prerequisites_raw: AC ENG 20C with a minimum grade of C- and AC ENG 22A . Placement via the UC Irvine Writing Placement Process

title: Introduction to Writing and Rhetoric with Lab
description: Introduces the principles of rhetoric through readings and writing assignments across a range of genres. Rigorous instruction in composition and style. Designed for students seeking additional English language support.
prerequisites_raw: AC ENG 20C with a minimum grade of C- and AC ENG 22A . Placement via the UC Irvine Writing Placement Process

title: Intensive Writing
description: Critical reading and analysis conducted through literary, academic, journalistic, and fictional genres with additional instruction in paragraph development and sentence-level mechanics. Students analyze and apply rhetorical principles in a range of writing assignments.
prerequisites_raw: AC ENG 20C with a minimum grade of C- and AC ENG 22A . Placement via the UC Irvine Writing Placement Process

title: Critical Reading and Rhetoric
description: Critical reading and analysis conducted through literary, academic, journalistic, and fictional genres. Students analyze and apply rhetorical principles in a range of writing assignments. Letter Grade with P/NP Option.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing requirement

title: Argument and Research
description: Intensive instruction in research methods, argumentation, and rhetorical invention. Readings selected from current nonfiction and materials located by students from the University library’s holdings, to include databases across a range of disciplines.
prerequisites_raw: WRITING 45 with a minimum grade of C or WRITING 50 with a minimum grade of C- or AP English Language and Composition with a minimum score of 4 or AP English Literature and Composition with a minimum score of 4

title: Intermediate Poetry Writing
description: Intermediate workshop in the writing of poetry, evaluation of student manuscripts, and parallel readings.
prerequisites_raw: WRITING 30 or WRITING 31

title: Intermediate Fiction Writing
description: Intermediate workshop in the writing of fiction, evaluation of student manuscripts, and parallel readings.
prerequisites_raw: WRITING 30 or WRITING 31

title: Undergraduate Seminar: Applications in Literary Theory and Criticism for Creative Writing
description: Readings in literature, with discussions and written rhetorical responses on their making.
prerequisites_raw: ( WRITING 30 or WRITING 31 ) and ( WRITING 90 or WRITING 91 ) and ( WRITING 30 or WRITING 31 or WRITING 90 or WRITING 91 or ENGLISH 16 or ENGLISH 17 ). Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Short Story Writing
description: Three-hour workshop in short fiction; discussion of student writing and of relevant literary texts.

title: Poetry Writing
description: Three-hour advanced poetry writing workshop; discussion of student writing and of relevant literary texts.

title: Novel Writing
description: Three-hour advanced workshop in fiction writing; discussion of student writing and of relevant literary texts.

title: Advanced Expository Writing
description: Study of rhetoric, disciplinary genres, and modes of knowledge production; practice in writing effective prose. Essays of varying lengths, totaling at least 4,000 words.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Writing Internship
description: Internships focused on writing. In consultation with a faculty advisor, students create a course from response essays, research essays, and assessment project data. Internships may include editing and publication projects, supervised teaching and tutoring assignments, community literacy projects.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement

title: Graduate Writers' Workshop (Fiction)
description: Graduate fiction workshop open to students enrolled in the MFA program in Writing.

title: Graduate Writers' Workshop (Fiction)
description: Graduate fiction workshop open to students enrolled in the MFA program in Writing.

title: Graduate Writers' Workshop (Poetry)
description: Graduate poetry workshop open to students enrolled in the M.F.A. Programs in Writing.

title: Writing in Conference (Fiction)
description: Graduate fiction workshop open to students enrolled in the MFA program in Writing.

title: Writing in Conference (Fiction)
description: Graduate fiction workshop open to students enrolled in the MFA program in Writing.
